title: Alice & Bob and ENS Lyon Demonstrate DC-Biased SQUID Architecture for Multi-Photon Cat Qubit Dissipation - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Alice & Bob and ENS Lyon showed that a microvolt-scale DC voltage bias across a SQUID coupler can replace microwave pump drives to stabilize cat qubits, averaging out parasitic Kerr nonlinearities. They demonstrated selectable 1-to-1, 2-to-1 and 4-to-1 photon conversion (18.2 MHz peak two-photon swap, 0.48 MHz dissipation), with implications for simpler wiring, lower cryostat heat load and four-component cat codes.

insights.claim: Standard cat-qubit stabilization uses strong microwave pump tones whose power introduces self-Kerr and cross-Kerr frequency shifts that degrade quantum state fidelity.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Identifies a core scaling limitation of the conventional cat-qubit approach that competitors must also solve.
insights.quote: high-power microwave pumping introduces unwanted self-Kerr and cross-Kerr non-linear frequency shifts that degrade quantum state fidelity

insights.claim: Alice & Bob and ENS Lyon replaced microwave parametric pumps with a microvolt-scale DC voltage bias across a SQUID, where tunneling Cooper pairs exchange 2eV energy and the continuously rotating Josephson frequency averages out first-order Kerr terms and flux detunings, keeping memory self-Kerr below 3 kHz.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A cleaner control mechanism strengthens Alice & Bob's bosonic-code path to fault tolerance.

insights.claim: Replacing microwave lines with DC bias wiring simplifies hardware layout and reduces heat loads inside dilution refrigerators.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Reduced wiring and cryogenic heat load addresses a key cost and scaling bottleneck for superconducting quantum systems.
insights.quote: Replacing microwave lines with DC voltage bias wiring simplifies hardware layout and reduces cryostat heat loads inside dilution refrigerators.

insights.claim: Coupling a 4.0429 GHz memory resonator to a 7.56 GHz buffer through a flux-tunable SQUID, the team achieved a peak two-photon swap rate of 18.2 MHz and an effective two-photon dissipation rate of 0.48 MHz, confirmed by Wigner tomography.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantitative benchmarks allow comparison with pump-based cat qubits; dissipation rate relative to errors will determine practical value.

insights.claim: Tuning the DC bias selectively activated 4-to-1 photon conversion, offering a direct pathway to four-component cat qubits that increase error protection without complex multi-frequency microwave control.

insights.so_what: Four-legged cat codes could expand the error-protection advantage of cat qubits, a potential differentiator for Alice & Bob.
